extName: Crate Bell - Sale alerts for Discogs
extDescription: One button to get an email when a record you want is for sale on Discogs. Simple, guided, free.
releaseAddAndAlert: Alert me when it's for sale
releaseHelpAdd: Adds it to your wantlist, then opens Discogs' alert page, filled in and ready to save.
releaseHelpSet: Get an email when a copy is listed. On the next page, you only click Save.
releaseHelpJustAdded: Added to your wantlist. Want an email when a copy is for sale?
releaseAddFailed: Crate Bell could not add this record to your wantlist. Check that you are logged in to Discogs, then try again.
releaseLoggedOut: Log in to Discogs to set sale alerts
emailOffShort: Sale alert emails are off on your Discogs account, so alerts cannot reach you.
masterTitle: Want any pressing of this album?
masterIntro: Discogs only emails you about records in your wantlist. Set one alert that covers every pressing you would accept.
masterLoadError: Crate Bell could not load the pressings of this album. Reload the page to try again.
masterStep1Title: Put those pressings in your wantlist
masterStep1Text: Discogs' Add to Wantlist menu, above the list of versions, can add every version at once. To be choosy, open a pressing and add it from its own page.
masterStep2Title: Set one alert for all of them
masterStep2Text: The alert only covers pressings that are in your wantlist.
masterTruncated: Discogs allows 100 filters per alert, so this alert covers the $1 oldest of the $2 pressings. Choose fewer formats to cover them all.
coachHelpTitle: What would you like to do?
coachHelpLimits: Discogs keeps up to $1 saved alerts per account, and up to $2 of them can send a daily email.
coachDelete1: Pick the alert in the Saved Searches list (circled in pink).
coachDelete3: Confirm. Discogs stops the emails for that alert straight away.
coachDeleteNote: Deleting an alert does not touch your wantlist.
coachDownText: The alert page did not load. This happens now and then on Discogs' side. Wait a minute, then reload.
coachSaveText: Your record is already selected on the left. Change the filters if you like, then open the save form.
coachSaveTextMaster: $1 pressings are selected on the left. Change the filters if you like, then open the save form.
coachTruncated: Some pressings were left out to stay within Discogs' limit of 100 filters per alert.
coachDrawerText: Crate Bell named your alert "$1" and chose $2. Change anything you like, then click Save Search at the bottom of the form.
frequencyRealtimeShort: an email as soon as a copy is listed
coachDrawerNote: Crate Bell never clicks Save for you. Your account, your decision.
coachEmailOff: Emails are off on your account, so this alert would stay silent. Click notification-settings in the form (circled in pink), tick Personal Email on the wantlist line, save, then come back.
coachError_digest_limit: You already have 30 alerts with a daily email, the most Discogs allows. Choose Realtime notifications instead, or delete an older daily alert.
coachError_filter_limit: This alert has more than 100 filters, the most Discogs allows. Remove a few filters on the left, then save again.
coachError_saved_limit: You have 300 saved alerts, the most Discogs allows. Delete an old one first: pick it in Saved Searches, then Delete.
coachError_name_too_long: The name is longer than 100 characters. Shorten it, then save again.
coachError_name_taken: You already have an alert with this name. Add a word to tell them apart, then save again.
coachDoneTextRealtime: Discogs will email you as soon as a copy of "$1" is listed.
coachDoneTextDigest: Discogs will include "$1" in your daily email when copies are listed.
coachDoneRemove: Once you buy it and add it to your collection, it leaves your wantlist and the emails stop. You can also delete the alert at any time from Saved Searches.
coffeeLine: Crate Bell is free and made by one collector.
coffeeTitle: Free, and made by a fellow collector
coffeeText: Crate Bell shows no ads and collects nothing. If it saves you time, you can buy me a coffee.
emailOnText: Discogs can email you when a record from your wantlist is listed.
emailOffText: Discogs will not email you, so sale alerts stay silent. Tick Personal Email on the line "When a release in my wantlist is listed for sale", then save.
emailLoggedOutText: Crate Bell could not read this setting. Open any Discogs page while logged in, then check again.
emailUnknownText: Open any Discogs page while logged in, or check now.
frequencyRealtimeText: One email per new listing. Best for rare records.
frequencyDigestText: A daily summary. Discogs allows $1 alerts like this.
prefsHideGeneric: Hide copies with a generic sleeve
prefsShipsFromHelp: Leave everything unticked to see copies from anywhere.
heroTitle: Never miss a record you want
heroLead: Crate Bell adds one pink button to Discogs. Click it on any record page and Discogs emails you when a copy goes on sale.
emailChapterText: Discogs sends sale alerts by email only. They need one box ticked in your Discogs notification settings: Personal Email, on the line "When a release in my wantlist is listed for sale". Crate Bell checks it for you below.
mockWantlistRow: When a release in my wantlist is listed for sale
mockOtherRow: When one of my orders needs feedback
mockSettingsCaption: In your Discogs notification settings, the Personal Email box on the wantlist line must be ticked. Then save at the bottom of the page.
howChapterTitle: Set an alert in three clicks
howChapterText: Alerts only work for records in your wantlist. Crate Bell adds the record for you when needed.
how1Text: On any record page, under Discogs' own buttons. If the record is not in your wantlist yet, Crate Bell adds it first.
how2Text: Discogs' alert page opens with your record and your usual filters already selected. A pink ring shows where to click.
how3Text: Crate Bell names the alert after the record and picks how often you want emails. Check it, then save. That is all.
masterGuideText: On an album's main page (Discogs calls it a master release), Crate Bell can set one alert for every pressing you would accept, for example all vinyl versions.
removeChapterTitle: How alerts stop, and how to remove one
removeStopTitle: They stop on their own when you buy
removeStopText1: Alerts only cover records in your wantlist. After a purchase, Discogs asks you to leave feedback and offers to add the record to your collection.
removeStopText2: Adding it to your collection takes it out of your wantlist, so the emails stop. The saved alert itself stays in your list, doing nothing, until you delete it.
removeDelete1: Open the Items I Want page on Discogs.
removeDelete2: In the left column, pick the alert in the Saved Searches list.
removeDelete4: Confirm. The emails for that alert stop.
removeDeleteNote: Deleting an alert does not remove the record from your wantlist. Discogs keeps up to 300 saved alerts per account.
prefsChapterText: Crate Bell applies these when it opens the alert page. You can still change them there, alert by alert.
faq1Q: Right away or once a day?
faq1A: Right away suits rare records: good copies can sell within hours. Once a day suits common ones. Discogs allows up to 30 alerts with a daily email; right-away alerts have no such limit.
faq2Q: Why do I have to click Save myself?
faq2A: Because it is your Discogs account. Crate Bell prepares everything and shows you where to click, but never acts without you.
faq3Q: What does Crate Bell know about me?
faq3A: Nothing leaves your browser. Your preferences are stored on this computer. Crate Bell only talks to Discogs, with your own session, to read the pages you visit and your email setting. No analytics, no ads.
faq4Q: Is Crate Bell made by Discogs?
faq4A: No. Crate Bell is an independent, open-source tool made by a collector. It is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, Discogs.
faq5A: Check three things: the setting in step 1 is on, the record is still in your wantlist, and the email is not in your spam folder. Discogs also skips listings that a seller simply put back online.
faq6A: Discogs changes its pages from time to time, and Crate Bell may then need an update.
